builder_evidence: Effects Database identifies Seamoon Inc. as a small Berkeley effects manufacturer and the Fresh Fuzz as its second release; Tone Machines documents Anderton and Lang hand-building the units; JHS independently identifies Seamoon's 1973 Fresh Fuzz as the source for its Berkeley tribute.
relationship_status: Designer identities and later JHS tribute are separate from the original builder. Production versions should later be modeled as product generations, not separate builders.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Promote as a historical California dirt builder.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents an original 1966 Carlsbro Fuzz-Tone and reports period advertising plus surviving factory documentation; the early unit is described as a Carlsbro-built three-transistor fuzz distinct from the later Sola Sound-supplied Carlsbro fuzz.
relationship_status: A later manufacturing transition to Sola Sound is explicitly documented. Do not attribute the later three-knob version to the same factory without dating evidence.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Preserve the 1966 Carlsbro-made fuzz as the primary qualification anchor and later Sola Sound production as a separate manufacturing relationship.

builder_evidence: TONEHOME identifies Lemon StudioSound as a Karlsruhe guitar-effects manufacturer founded by Gerard Daleiden in the 1970s and documents the Zuzz Thainer as a combined fuzz/sustainer/noise-gate product from the 1977-1978 period.
relationship_status: No qualification-critical OEM relationship is required. The catalog can later be expanded from period catalog scans.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Already present as a discovered builder; qualification is now explicitly audited.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents Jennings Electronic Developments/Industries producing distinctive fuzz and other guitar effects from 1968 into the early 1970s, with surviving JED and JEI fuzz examples and period trade-show/press evidence.
relationship_status: JED and JEI are name states of the Jennings lineage rather than separate builders; exact assembly staffing remains a later research question.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Treat JED/JEI as one dated builder lineage.

builder_evidence: Morley's own history credits Ray with creating the Power Wah Fuzz, and GuitarPlayer identifies Tel-Ray Electronics as the original manufacturer of Morley pedals while documenting the PWF as a 1970s product.
relationship_status: Tel-Ray manufacturer identity and Morley marketing identity are deliberately separated. Corporate succession and the later Morley Product Group are outside qualification scope.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Keep Morley/Tel-Ray as a manufacturer lineage record.

builder_evidence: TONEHOME documents fOXX pedals made by Ridinger Associates Inc. in Chatsworth, California, including the Clean Machine, a dedicated overdrive/fuzz device; Danelectro's current history identifies Steve Ridinger as the creator of the 1970s FOXX pedal line.
relationship_status: Trademark ownership and modern Danelectro revival identity are separate from original 1970s manufacture.
recommended_treatment: Builder census eligible. Preserve fOXX as product/brand identity and Ridinger Associates as manufacturer identity.

builder_evidence: Fuzzboxes documents a May 1966 advertisement for a Kelly Fuzz Box and family testimony suggesting Kelly may have built the boxes, while also acknowledging a possible Macari/Sola Sound supply arrangement.
relationship_status: Physical manufacturing remains unresolved and no surviving Kelly Fuzz exemplar is known. This is exactly the kind of relationship ambiguity the hard qualification gate should block from verified status.
recommended_treatment: Keep research-only/provisional. Do not promote until direct manufacturing evidence emerges.
